Ford, EPA and Haynes do call it the F-250, but Wikipedia and Haynes treat it as a different truck from the old-body F-250 Heavy Duty, so it belongs with the 1997+ F-150 page.

notes: Ford F-250 3/4-ton, 2WD and 4WD, 1953-1997 (the old-body F-250 Heavy Duty ended with 1997; there is no 1998 old-body F-250 HD). NHRA has no F-250 rows. independent_sources counts distinct groups: all Ford material = 1, Hagerty, BlueOvalTech, Wikipedia (all articles = 1), EPA (1984+, under 8,500 lb GVWR only, so it never covers the F-250HD), Haynes. Status: three_sources_not_nhra = 3+ groups; two_sources_agree = exactly 2 reputable groups agree exactly; two_sources_not_nhra = 2 groups, rating not matched; single_source = 1. Status describes whether the engine was offered; hp is null where sources give conflicting ratings and no figure can be checked (per the source rule), with the figures in note. Gross hp through 1971, SAE net from 1972. F-250HD (1982-1997, over 8,500 lb GVWR) engines are recorded with trims 'F-250HD'. F-350-only engines not recorded: 6.6L/400 in 1980-81 (Ford 1980/1981 charts, BlueOvalTech, Hagerty: F-350 only); 'heavy-duty' 181-hp 272 (1957, F-350 dual-rear); F-Super Duty chassis-cab engines. The 1998 model year is listed with no engines: Wikipedia and a Diesel Hub timeline say 1997 was the last old-body F-250 (no 1998 F-Series 7.3), Hagerty has no 1998 F-250 or F-350, and Ford's 1998 F-Series brochure shows only the new-body light-duty F-250. Haynes (2019) says the opposite, that only the F-250 HD stayed on the old platform for 1998. Hagerty has no 1953-56 or 1961-66 F-250, and its pre-1961 hp figures are not factory gross ratings.
